vrijens-2012.title: A new taxonomy for describing and defining adherence to medications

quotes.text: The process by which patients take their medications as prescribed, composed of initiation, implementation and discontinuation.
Initiation occurs when the patient takes the first dose of a prescribed medication.
Implementation is the extent to which a patient’s actual dosing corresponds to the prescribed dosing regimen, from initiation until the last dose.
Discontinuation occurs when the patient stops taking the prescribed medication, for whatever reason(s).
Persistence is the length of time between initiation and the last dose, which immediately precedes discontinuation.
Discontinuation marks the end of therapy, when the next dose to be taken is omitted and no more doses are taken thereafter.
The quantification of implementation requires the comparison of two time-series: the prescribed drug dosing regimen and the patient’s drug dosing history.

The most frequent summary statistics for quantifying, within a patient, the implementation of a dosing regimen, over a defined interval of time, are: 1 the proportion of prescribed drug taken; 2 the proportion of days with the correct number of doses taken;

vrijens-2012.supports: What the History screen's adherence figure measures: implementation, as doses taken over doses due across a window of finished days (adherence, medAdherence, dailyShares in stats.ts over dueDoses in schedule.ts). Discontinuation and persistence are why stopping a medication ends its schedule (endDate, endCourse) instead of deleting it, so the history it earned keeps scoring against the schedule that existed then.

summary.en: The standard meaning of taking a medicine as prescribed. The History percentage is the share of the doses your schedule asked for that you marked as taken; stopping a medicine ends its schedule, not its history.

vrijens-2012.note: Published version (with journal pagination) read from the University of Liège repository copy, https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/305261/1/Vrijens__2012_GDO_BJCP.pdf; the PMC record is PMC3403197. The taxonomy came from a systematic literature review followed by discussion with international experts (the ABC Project). Crossref lists the fourth author as 'Przemyslaw Kardas' with given and family names swapped; the paper prints 'Kardas Przemyslaw'. Table 2's implementation definition ends 'until the last dose'; the body text on p. 696 ends 'until the last dose is taken'. The app's rule that a dose deliberately set aside leaves both numerator and denominator (countedDoses) is the app's own choice, not the taxonomy's: the paper counts any dose the prescribed regimen asked for, and lists a skipped dose as a deviation in implementation.

lakemedelsverket-2026-lakemedelsfakta.title: Sök läkemedelsfakta

quotes.text: Sök läkemedelsfakta är en söktjänst som innehåller information om alla godkända och registrerade läkemedel och substanser för människor och djur i Sverige.

Alla läkemedel som finns i handeln måste vara godkända eller registrerade av Läkemedelsverket. I Läkemedelsfakta finns information om alla godkända och registrerade läkemedel, tillfälligt återkallade läkemedel samt alla läkemedel som har avregistrerats efter 1 juli 2004.
Ett läkemedel kan förekomma i flera olika styrkor, till exempel 500 mg eller 5 %.
Alvedon 500 mg filmdragerad tablett
Alvedon forte 1 g filmdragerad tablett
Trombyl 75 mg tablett
Trombyl 160 mg tablett
Eliquis 2,5 mg filmdragerad tablett
Eliquis 5 mg filmdragerad tablett

lakemedelsverket-2026-lakemedelsfakta.supports: The public record the bundled catalog's names and strengths come from (src/app/data/medications.ts): each entry is a name as printed on the box with strengths Läkemedelsverket lists for it.

summary.en: The Swedish Medical Products Agency's public record of approved medicines, where the names and strengths the medication form suggests come from. The suggestions only help you type; a medicine not on the list works the same.

lakemedelsverket-2026-lakemedelsfakta.note: The service is a script-driven page; the first three quotes are from the page's embedded help text and the product lines are the server-rendered page titles of each product page. Checked 2026-09-27 against the product records (api/lmfrest/medprod): Alvedon 500 mg, Alvedon forte 1 g, Trombyl 75 mg and 160 mg, Eliquis 2,5 mg and 5 mg are 'Godkänd' and 'Säljs'. The 665 mg modified-release paracetamol tablet (Alvedon 665 mg, id 20030307000193) is 'Tillfälligt återkallad' / 'Säljs inte', so that strength was removed from the Alvedon, Panodil and Paracetamol entries under the catalog's 'currently-dispensed medications only' rule. One remaining difference: the 1 g tablet is sold as 'Alvedon forte', not plain 'Alvedon'. The catalog writes '2.5 mg' where Läkemedelsverket writes '2,5 mg'.

lakemedelsverket-2026-npl.title: Nationellt produktregister för läkemedel, NPL

quotes.text: Nationellt produktregister för läkemedel, NPL, är ett register med information om samtliga läkemedel som är godkända eller registrerade i Sverige.
Läkemedelsverket förvaltar NPL och ser till att informationen i registret är korrekt. Den utgör den grundläggande informationskällan för läkemedelsprodukter som används i Sverige.
NPL är öppet för alla besökare från Sverige och det krävs ingen registrering för att ladda hem eller använda det.
Delar av produktinformationen i NPL är sökbar i Läkemedelsfakta.

lakemedelsverket-2026-npl.supports: The open national register the catalog would be regenerated from (the header of src/app/data/medications.ts names Läkemedelsverket's LiiV/NPL data), downloaded into the bundle rather than queried, since the app makes no lookup calls.

summary.en: The national register of every medicine approved in Sweden, the open data a fuller list of suggestions would be built from.

lakemedelsverket-2026-npl.note: Page last changed 2026-06-21; the current export is NPL 4.5 (released 2025-02-21). The export host npl.mpa.se could not be reached from the research environment, so no product was checked against the export itself.

nlm-2025-rxnorm.title: RxNorm

quotes.text: RxNorm provides normalized names for clinical drugs and links its names to many of the drug vocabularies commonly used in pharmacy management and drug interaction software, including those of First Databank, Micromedex, Multum, and Gold Standard Drug Database.
RxNorm contains the names of prescription and many over-the-counter drugs available in the United States.
lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet
levothyroxine sodium 0.05 MG Oral Tablet
acetaminophen 500 MG Oral Tablet
metformin hydrochloride 500 MG Oral Tablet

nlm-2025-rxnorm.supports: The record the US catalog's names and strengths come from (src/app/data/medications-us.ts): each entry is a generic name with strengths RxNorm lists as clinical drugs of that ingredient, restated the way a US label writes them.

summary.en: The U.S. National Library of Medicine's standard names for the medicines sold in the United States, where the names and strengths the medication form suggests on an American phone come from. The suggestions only help you type; a medicine not on the list works the same.

nlm-2025-rxnorm.note: The overview page was last reviewed 2025-11-19. Checked 2026-09-28 through the RxNav API (drugs.json, clinical drugs): every strength in the catalog matches an RxNorm clinical drug of the same ingredient, allowing for RxNorm's units (50 mcg is 0.05 MG; 1% is 10 MG/ML; 90 mcg a puff is 0.09 MG/ACTUAT) and its ingredient names (divalproex is 'divalproex sodium', alendronate 'alendronic acid', B12 'vitamin B12'). The catalog leaves out brand names and every medicine on the DEA's controlled-substance schedules; that is the app's curation choice, not RxNorm's.
